answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond in the umber registry and files a log with checkpoint signals, each for its segment. An auditor checks it against every prior log in the garden, so the kth identity pays 2 credits per prior entry, or 2(k-1) credits. A segment without a matching signal burns 40 credits and rejects the identity. Rented logs fail: signals bind to the applicant key and cannot be replayed. For 1,000 fakes, bonds lock 80,000 credits and audit fees total 999,000 credits. An honest agent files one log, pays one audit fee, and reclaims its bond after one epoch.
